extra_misconceptions.fact: Every dollar of space agency funding is paid to earthly engineers, manufacturers, and labs that create local jobs and technology.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Money spent on space missions is launched into orbit and removed from the domestic economy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: All three products were invented prior to Apollo, though NASA popularized them by using them extensively during crewed spaceflights.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Velcro, Tang, and Teflon were invented from scratch by NASA engineers for the Apollo moon landings.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Multispectral sensors measure infrared, radar, and microwave wavelengths to map ocean salinity, soil moisture, and polar ice thickness.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Earth-observing satellites only take visible-light photographs of clouds to help television meteorologists.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The 1967 Outer Space Treaty forbids any nation from claiming sovereignty over celestial bodies and reserves space for peaceful exploration.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: International space treaties allow the first nation that lands on the Moon or an asteroid to claim sovereign territory.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes a cold-war prestige objective from a modern scientific goal in deep-space missions?
Which orbital measurement helps scientists track groundwater depletion and crop health across continents?
Under what condition does sharing spacecraft docking standards improve crew rescue options in low Earth orbit?
What specific evidence shows that a consumer product originated as a NASA spinoff rather than a terrestrial invention?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Goddard's March 1926 rocket rose only 41 feet during a 2.5-second flight, yet it proved liquid propulsion was practical.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Robert Goddard's first liquid-fueled rocket flew several miles high into the upper stratosphere in 1926.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Tsiolkovsky was a theoretical physicist who derived the rocket equation on paper decades before Sergei Korolev built Soviet launchers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky built and launched the first Soviet orbital rockets from Baikonur Cosmodrome.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mathematicians, flight directors, propulsion engineers, and mission planners are equally vital pioneers in aerospace history.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Space pioneers only include astronauts and cosmonauts who physically rode rockets above the Karman line.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth first in April 1961, while Alan Shepard flew a 15-minute suborbital trajectory three weeks later.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Alan Shepard was the first human in space and completed three full orbits during the Freedom 7 flight.

extra_socratic_questions: What engineering breakthrough separates Robert Goddard's 1926 Auburn launch from earlier black-powder fireworks?
Which mathematical contribution by Konstantin Tsiolkovsky still governs propellant mass ratios on modern launch vehicles?
Where did Katherine Johnson's trajectory calculations prove critical when electronic computers failed or needed verification?
What archival sources verify the exact flight duration, apogee, and mission role listed on the back of your pioneer card?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The letter C indicates double the total impulse of a B motor, while the number 6 shows both motors have the same 6-newton average thrust.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A C6-5 model rocket motor produces twice the peak thrust of a B6-4 motor at liftoff.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Biodegradable flameproof wadding shields the plastic parachute or streamer from hot gases when the ejection charge fires at apogee.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Recovery wadding is stuffed into the body tube primarily to add nose weight and shift the center of gravity.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The NAR Safety Code requires removing the safety interlock key and waiting a full 60 seconds before approaching any misfired rocket.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A misfired model rocket can be approached immediately after releasing the electrical launch controller button.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A glued nose cone blocks the ejection charge from deploying the parachute and causes a dangerous high-speed ballistic impact.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Gluing the nose cone permanently to the body tube makes the rocket stronger for its second flight objective.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a rocket's flight path when the center of pressure sits ahead of the center of gravity?
Which physical indicator on a model rocket engine code tells you the delay time before ejection charge ignition?
Why is it dangerous to omit flameproof recovery wadding between the motor mount and the plastic parachute?
What measurement confirms the launch rod angle and minimum standoff distance required by the NAR Safety Code?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rockets accelerate by Newton's third law, throwing exhaust mass backward at high speed and working even more efficiently in a vacuum.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rocket engines generate forward motion by pushing their exhaust gases against the surrounding air or launch pad.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Gravity at the space station's altitude is still about 90 percent of surface gravity, but the craft is in continuous sideways free-fall.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Astronauts and satellites float in low Earth orbit because Earth's gravity drops to zero above the atmosphere.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Spacecraft sensors convert light pixels into binary numbers and transmit the data via radio waves to Deep Space Network antennas.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Deep-space probes drop physical film canisters back to Earth whenever they photograph outer planets.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Once at orbital velocity in near-vacuum, a satellite coasts by inertia and only fires thrusters occasionally to counter slight air drag.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Satellites in low Earth orbit must fire their main engines continuously to keep from falling back to the ground.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a rocket's thrust in the vacuum of space where there is no atmospheric air to push against?
Under what condition does a satellite's forward tangential velocity match the curvature of Earth's gravitational pull?
Why must a chemical rocket carry its own oxidizer tank while a commercial jet aircraft uses only fuel tanks?
What happens to a digital image between a spacecraft's optical sensor and a Deep Space Network dish on Earth?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Radio signals take between 4 and 24 minutes one way to reach Mars, so rovers execute pre-programmed command sequences autonomously.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Engineers on Earth drive Mars rovers in real time using live video and a joystick from mission control.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Flybys capture brief wide-area snapshots, orbiters map global terrain over years, and landers perform direct chemical contact tests.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Robotic flyby missions and orbital missions collect the exact same surface mineralogy data as a lander.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sunlight is too weak in the outer solar system, so both Voyager probes use radioisotope thermoelectric generators fueled by plutonium.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 use large solar arrays to power their instruments in the Kuiper Belt and beyond.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Apollo astronauts deployed seismometers and laser retroreflectors that still measure the Moon's distance and internal structure today.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Apollo missions only collected photographs and left no active scientific instruments on the lunar surface.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does a mission planner choose an uncrewed robotic probe over a human expedition?
What geological discovery from the Apollo lunar rock samples changed how scientists explain the Moon's origin?
Which physical indicator in Mars rover core samples points to ancient liquid water lakes in Jezero Crater?
What communication delay measurement limits real-time joystick control of a robotic rover on Mars or Titan?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Reentry heat comes mainly from rapid air compression in the shock wave ahead of the blunt heat shield as the vehicle decelerates.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Atmospheric reentry heating is caused primarily by skin friction rubbing against air molecules.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The external liquid-propellant tank was the only non-reusable major Shuttle component and burned up over the ocean after launch.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Space Shuttle's giant orange external tank was launched into orbit and reused on every mission.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Over 40 assembly flights across more than a decade were required to connect the station's pressurized modules and truss segments.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The International Space Station was launched into orbit fully assembled atop a single heavy-lift rocket.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Alongside the solar wings, the station uses large white accordion-like radiator panels to reject waste heat into the vacuum of space.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Large gold-colored panels extending from the International Space Station are all photovoltaic solar arrays.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a crewed capsule's kinetic energy during atmospheric reentry if the thermal protection shield fails?
Which environmental control subsystem removes exhaled carbon dioxide so astronauts do not suffocate inside a sealed cabin?
Where does the International Space Station store electrical power during the 35 minutes of each orbit spent in Earth's shadow?
What structural distinction separates a reusable winged orbiter from a capsule that lands under parachutes?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The Martian atmosphere is less than 1 percent as dense as Earth's and lacks a global magnetic field, requiring regolith or subsurface shielding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mars has a thick enough carbon dioxide atmosphere to shield surface habitats from cosmic radiation without extra cover.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Titan sits nearly ten times farther from the Sun and beneath a thick nitrogen haze, receiving less than 1 percent of Earth's sunlight.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Solar panels on Saturn's moon Titan generate the same wattage per square meter as solar arrays in Earth orbit.

extra_misconceptions.fact: In-situ resource utilization extracts water ice and oxygen from local regolith and prints structural shields from native surface soil.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All building concrete, drinking water, and breathing oxygen for a planetary base must be launched from Earth.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unshielded surface glass admits lethal cosmic rays and micrometeoroids, so habitats use buried growth chambers with LED lighting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Large glass greenhouses on the surface of the Moon can use unfiltered sunlight for crops without radiation danger.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to rely solely on solar panels for a habitat built on Saturn's moon Titan or during a lunar night?
Where should a Scout position regolith shielding on a lunar or Martian habitat to block solar particle events?
What closed-loop recycling rate in your habitat's water system reduces the mass of resupply rockets from Earth?
Under what condition does an airlock decompression protocol protect the rest of the base during a suit leak?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Space programs depend on machinists, avionics technicians, software developers, space medicine doctors, and planetary geologists.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Only astronauts and degreed aeronautical engineers can find full-time employment in the space industry.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most aerospace professionals work for commercial launch providers, satellite manufacturers, defense contractors, or research universities.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every aerospace career in the United States requires working directly for NASA as a federal civil servant.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most entry-level aerospace engineers begin work with an ABET-accredited bachelor's degree and hands-on internship or club experience.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A doctoral degree is mandatory before applying for any entry-level spacecraft engineering or mission operations job.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Youth Protection guidelines require parent or guardian permission and two-deep leadership or a parent present for any career interview.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scouts can schedule private one-on-one video interviews with industry professionals without involving a parent.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes the daily responsibilities of a flight dynamics officer from those of a propulsion test engineer?
Which accreditation standard confirms that a university aerospace engineering program meets industry licensing rules?
Under what condition does an aerospace technician need a federal security clearance or export-control verification?
What safety protocol must a Scout follow before contacting an aerospace professional for a career interview?
